1. Background

One of the key recommendations of the High Level Committee on the Economic Impact of COVID-19, headed by Dr.C.Rangarajan, is the urgent need to introduce a “Wage Employment Programme” for Urban Poor to create employment opportunity through provision of daily wages. The Vision Document for a New Dawn also envisages extension of the Wage Employment Programme to Urban areas. Though the report of the High Level Committee relates to mitigating the adverse impact of COVID-19, the recommendation of the Committee is still relevant to improve the livelihood of Urban Poor and to provide a safety net against loss of job. As per the BPL survey conducted in ULBs during the year 2015 by Commissionerate of Municipal Administration for the implementation of Urban Poverty Alleviation Scheme the urban poor constitute nearly 38% of the total population.

2. Objectives and Goals

The primary objective of the scheme is to enhance livelihood opportunities in the urban areas by providing or enabling employment to every household whose adult members seek to do_ unskilled, semiskilled and skilled work. Creation of infrastructure, such as natural resource management works, flood mitigation works and the works for protection of the environment and greening of urban space; increasing urban consumption expenditure; promoting social and gender equity; and empowerment of women are important supplementary objectives. The major goals aimed are;

i) Improving Livelihood and Social Security by increasing employment opportunities.

ii) Facilitating employment opportunities appropriate to the skill levels.

iii) | Creation and maintenance of Public Assets.

iv) Greening and protection of the environment.

v) Undertaking works related to natural resource management.

3. Applicability and Selection Criteria

The scheme will be implemented in two zones in Greater Chennai Corporation, one zone each in 14 Corporations, one Municipality each

in 7 Regions (7 Municipalities) and one Town Panchayat each in 37 Districts (37 Town Panchayats) in Tamil Nadu during the year 2021-22.

In respect of GCC and other Corporations, zones will be selected based on prevalence of poverty and gap in infrastructure facilities / basic amenities. The Municipalities will be selected based on prevalence of poverty, vicinity to rural area and lack of infrastructure facilities/ amenities. extracts.text:
Section Officer

ANNEXURE

Guidelines for the Implementation of Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam (KNMT)

1. Introduction

In Tamil Nadu, there are 14 Corporations (except Greater Chennai Corporation), 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats. Many schemes taken up in the recent years such as Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT are aimed at improving the infrastructure facilities of Corporations and major towns alone. Smart Cities Mission is being implemented only in 11 Corporations. AMRUT is also being implemented in 28 Towns only. The coverage of schemes in Corporations is relatively high when compared to Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Hence it has been decided to introduce a new Scheme “Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam”’(KNMT) in all 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats so as to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in these Urban Local

Bodies. 2. Implementation Plan

The vision of the Government is providing water service connection to all urban house holds, safe sewer disposal to each household either through UGSS or through FSTP, street lights and good road facilities. Though there are schemes for the provision of 100% functional household tap connections, sewer links, roads, such are highly capital intensive, mostly covering only prominent areas in the Urban Local Bodies. Infrastructure gaps remain existing in many backward areas/ slums and also newly added areas of the Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Considering the above factors, it has been decided to give preference to the slum areas/ backward areas and added areas of the ULBs for the implementation of KNMT.

2.1 Urban Development Plan (UDP)

The distribution of basic amenities is not uniform across the Urban Local Bodies and in certain wards / specific areas, the basic amenities are still inadequate. In order to have an equitable distribution of basic amenities, a detailed survey will be conducted and an Urban Development Plan (UDP) will be prepared for each urban local body so as to assess the present availability of basic infrastructure and the gaps

to be fulfilled.

The detailed survey will be conducted ward wise, with respect to the availability of water supply, sanitation, internal roads, street lights,

burial ground / crematorium availability and other community infrastructure. With regard to roads, a detailed Roads Network Plan will be prepared indicating all the major roads maintained by various agencies viz National Highways, State Highways and Municipalities / Town Panchayats (Access roads and internal streets) in the Urban Local Bodies concerned. With respect to water supply, the total demand, including the present supply and the future requirement will be taken into account and incorporated. Based on this, a “City Water balance Plan” will be prepared for each Urban Local Body. Similar survey and assessment of the gaps will be undertaken for all needed components of the ULBs concerned.

extracts.text:
Section Officer

ANNEXURE

Guidelines for Implementation of Namakku Naame Thittam (Urban)

People’s participation is essential in civic infrastructure projects. It

also brings the sense of ownership among the people. In order to improve the self-support mechanism of public and to enhance increased public participation in creating and maintaining community infrastructure, the Government has proposed to introduce the Namakku Naame Thittam (Urban) from 2021-22 onwards.

Namakku Naame Thittam (Urban) will be implemented in all Urban

local bodies, viz Greater Chennai Corporation, all 14 Corporations, all 121 Municipalities and in all 528 Town Panchayats.

1. Public Participation :

>

>

>

The minimum public contribution for any of the identified work should be one third of the estimate value.

In respect of the works related to renovation of water bodies, the minimum public contribution should be 50% for the desilting and bund formation component. For other components like pathway, retaining wall, light / bench facilities etc, the minimum public contribution will be one third of estimate value.

There will be no upper limit for public contribution.

2. Procedure for Selection of Works:

(i) The proposal for taking up of works under Namakku Naame

Thittam (Urban) may originate from individuals, groups, such as resident welfare association, institutions, public or private companies or from the community.

(ii) Request in the form of an application indicating the work to be

taken up with consent for contributing at least one-third of the estimate amount by the public has to be given to the concerned Commissioners (in case of Corporation / Municipalities) or Executive officers (in case of Town Panchayats).

(iii) The Commissioners / Executive officers after ascertaining the need

and feasibility of the proposed work with reference to the norms of the scheme, will ask for the detailed estimate from the implementing agency. Thereafter, the applicant should deposit the prescribed amount with the concerned urban local body.

(iv) The contribution by industries, companies and other entities may be accepted as public contribution. The contributions made by any entity under CSR may also be accepted as public contribution, subject to instructions contained in the Letter (Ms) No.310,Finance (BPE)/2020, Dated 31.7.2020.

(v) Local body fund / grant cannot be taken as Public contribution.

(vi) If permission of any other department, other than urban local bodies concerned, is necessary to execute the work, permission shall be obtained from the concerned department before according Administrative Sanction.

(vii) If the assets to be created have to be maintained by any other department, concurrence should be obtained from the department concerned.
